name: Voice
summary: Hears you and answers out loud, with Whisper and Piper running on this machine — and, if you give it a key, a voice cloned from a clip of your own.

requires.why: To hear you when you speak. The recording is turned into text here and the sound is not kept.
To read an answer out loud through your speakers.
To open a recording you point it at.
To keep Whisper and the speech model in a folder of its own.
To fetch Whisper and Piper once from GitHub, and a speech model and a voice once from Hugging Face.
To run Whisper and Piper here rather than sending anything away to be listened to or read out.
To browse the voices published on fish.audio and to speak in one, and only once you have added a key.

settings.label: Speech model
settings.hint: Bigger is more accurate and slower. Tiny is 75 MB, base 148 MB, small 488 MB.

settings.label: Processor threads
settings.hint: More is faster until it is not. Four suits most machines.

settings.label: Whisper program
settings.hint: Leave this empty and Alexia downloads one. Point it at your own whisper-cli if you have a build that suits this machine better.

settings.label: Piper program
settings.hint: The same again for speaking. Empty means Alexia fetches one; on a machine with no prebuilt Piper this is how you supply your own.

settings.label: fish.audio key
settings.hint: Only needed to clone a voice from a recording, which Piper cannot do. Leave it empty and everything stays on this machine.

settings.label: A recording to clone
settings.hint: Fifteen seconds of the voice you want, as a .wav. Put the words that were said in the box below, then press Clone on the Voice panel.

settings.label: What the recording says
settings.placeholder: The exact words spoken in the clip.
settings.hint: A cloner told what was said makes a better voice than one guessing.

settings.label: Speak with expression
settings.hint: Marks a reply up with emotion before it is spoken. Costs one small model call per reply, and only works with a cloned voice — Piper has no expression at all.

settings.label: Download now
settings.hint: Fetches Whisper, Piper, the speech model and the voice. It happens on first use anyway; this is for getting it over with while you are looking.

settings.label: Add a voice
settings.hint: A Piper .onnx voice you have downloaded, with its .onnx.json beside it. Point at it here, then press Add on the Voice panel.

widgets.label: Voices
widgets.hint: Which voice speaks, and what else this machine has. A published voice downloads the first time it is used.

widgets.label: Add the voice in the box
widgets.hint: Copies the file named in “Add a voice”, on the plugins screen, into Alexia. Piper does not clone a voice from a recording — this is for a voice you have already downloaded.

widgets.label: Clone the voice in the recording
widgets.hint: Uses the recording and the words named on the plugins screen. Needs a fish.audio key: the clip and its transcript leave this machine, and the voice lives on that account until you remove it here.

widgets.label: Find a voice
widgets.hint: A name to look for among the voices published on fish.audio. Leave it empty to see what the filters alone turn up.

widgets.label: Language
widgets.hint: Language codes. Most of the catalogue is not English, so leaving all of them off answers in languages you cannot judge.

widgets.label: Kind of voice
widgets.hint: The vendor's own words for its voices. Several together narrow it.

widgets.label: Search fish.audio
widgets.hint: Asks again with whatever is in the boxes above, and fills the list below.

widgets.label: Voices on fish.audio
widgets.hint: The top five for what you searched. Hear one, then keep it — a kept voice joins the list above and can speak, without ever being downloaded.
